Classification table of a choice model

Source: R/compare.R
classification.Rd

Cross-tabulates the chosen alternative against the modal predicted alternative (weighted by the frequency weights), with the share correctly classified and the proportional reduction in error relative to always predicting the most frequent alternative. Modal classification understates a model's value for minority alternatives: a case with probability 0.4 on a rare alternative is classified to the common one even though 0.4 may be far above its base rate; see the probability-based measures in fit_stats().

Usage

classification(object, newdata = NULL, weights = NULL, offset = NULL)

Arguments

object

A "choicemodel" fit.

newdata

Optional data frame (same layout as the fit) with the response; default the estimation cases. A hold-out set may lack some alternative or covariate level; only the response and the predictors are read from it.

weights

Optional frequency weights for newdata (a column name or a vector aligned to its rows); the estimation cases use the fit's weights.

offset

Offset for newdata when the fit has one (see predict.choicemodel()).

Value

An object of class "pc_classification": a list with table (observed in rows, predicted in columns), correct, and pre.

See also

fit_stats()

Other model comparison: boot_lr_test(), compare_models(), fit_stats(), lr_test(), vuong()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(800, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
classification(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#>         predicted
#> observed   a   b   c
#>        a   0  98  89
#>        b   0 347  46
#>        c   0  73 147
#> 
#> Correctly classified: 0.618; proportional reduction in error over the modal alternative: 0.248
